summary.en: Order whole records by stable low-to-high digit passes with explicit key encoding and digit bounds.
summary.bn: ছোট digit থেকে stable counting pass চালিয়ে পূর্ণ key সাজাও।

notes: C17 baseline; general algorithm bounds treat input size as variable.

examples.title: Order five marks, including a tie
examples.explanationHtml: Shifted keys 106,102,104,102,100 are ordered with three decimal passes. The original values finish as 1 3 3 5 7.

examples.title: Sort numbers entered at the keyboard
examples.explanationHtml: Adding 99 gives a nonnegative digit representation even for -2. Stable digit passes retain all original signed values.

examples.title: Use sorted neighbours to find distinct marks
examples.explanationHtml: After the digit passes, equal original scores are adjacent. The distinct-group scan therefore reports three.

examples.title: Watch values cross decimal boundaries
examples.explanationHtml: The shifted keys span 0, 1, 99, 198 and 100. Units order alone is not final; later stable passes settle tens and hundreds.

practice.title: Perform only the encoded units pass
practice.statementHtml: Apply one stable radix pass using the units digit of key + 99. Print Enter n, then n values:, read n (0..64) and keys -99..99, and display the resulting original keys on one line. Do not run tens or hundreds passes.
hints: Extract encoded digits, but copy whole original values to output.

practice.title: Display negative keys after all digit passes
practice.statementHtml: Run all three radix passes on the shifted encoding, then display only original negative values in ascending order. Input follows Enter n, then n values: and consists of n (0..64) plus n keys (-99..99). If none are negative, print an empty result line.
hints: Sort by encoded digits first, then stop the displayed prefix at zero.

practice.title: Explain the Radix Sort invariant
practice.statementHtml: For Radix Sort, state what stays true as the main process repeats. Explain the start, preservation and completed result.
hints: Use the changing boundaries and the processed region in this method.
practice.answerHtml:
Assume the array is sorted by the first r processed low digits. A stable pass on digit r + 1 orders records by that new digit. Within each equal new-digit group, the earlier order by the r lower digits remains unchanged. Hence the array is sorted by the combined r + 1 low digits. The base before any pass is vacuous, and after all digits this order is the full encoded-key order.

Adding 99 is strictly increasing over the permitted original range, so encoded-key order equals original-key order. Each pass preserves all whole records through a separate output buffer. The fixed three-pass loop terminates without relying on an unbounded power calculation.

practice.title: Derive the resource cost of Radix Sort
practice.statementHtml: Include digit count d and base b, then explain why pass buffers need not coexist.
hints: Count the work from this algorithm rather than naming a class alone.
practice.answerHtml: The demonstration has b = 10 and d = 3, so its time is Θ(3(n + 10)) and its peak auxiliary space is Θ(n + 10). The general expression Θ(d(n + b)) must stay visible when key width or base can vary. Stability is inherited from each counting pass, and the shared output buffer means the method is not in-place under a constant-workspace definition.

practice.title: Reconstruct the small radix sort trace
practice.statementHtml: For [7,3,5,3,1], encode keys with +99 and apply stable decimal LSD passes at 1, 10 and 100. Show the original-value order after each pass.
hints: Record state before changing another boundary or moving the next value.
practice.answerHtml:
StageStateReason
Encode[106,102,104,102,100]Add 99 only for digit extraction.
Units pass[1,3,3,5,7]Digits 0,2,2,4,6 determine the record order.
Tens pass[1,3,3,5,7]Equal tens digits retain units order.
Hundreds pass[1,3,3,5,7]Equal leading digits retain the final ascending order.

quiz.prompt: In LSD radix sort, which digit is handled first?
options: The least significant digit
The most significant digit
A random digit
Only the middle digit
quiz.explanation: Later stable passes preserve the ordering built by lower digits.

quiz.prompt: Why must each radix digit pass be stable?
options: It makes the buffer constant size
Equal current digits must preserve earlier lower-digit order
All digit values must be unique
It avoids reading the input
quiz.explanation: Stability is what combines individual digit orders correctly.

quiz.prompt: For key 472 and place 10, which digit is extracted?
quiz.explanation: Integer division gives 47 and remainder ten selects 7.

quiz.prompt: What is the general radix time for d passes and base b?
options: Theta(n) regardless of d and b
Theta(n log n) always
Theta(b^n)
Theta(d(n + b))
quiz.explanation: Each counting pass scans n records and b counter slots.

quiz.prompt: Why does adding 99 preserve the order of -99..99?
options: The same addition is strictly increasing
Every key becomes the same
The sign bit disappears by magic
It swaps the maximum and minimum
quiz.explanation: For any x < y, x + 99 < y + 99.

quiz.prompt: Why is radix workspace not multiplied by the number of passes?
options: Each pass uses no output
The same-sized output and counters can be reused
Only one record ever moves
Previous buffers are all required forever
quiz.explanation: Peak live storage is one pass buffer plus counters.

quiz.prompt: What is wrong with calling radix sort always linear in n?
options: It cannot preserve duplicates
It never terminates for fixed digits
Digit count or base may grow with the key domain
Its keys are always arbitrary objects
quiz.explanation: The full bound retains d and b as parameters.

quiz.prompt: What tens digit does radix extraction obtain from 472?
quiz.explanation: Division leaves 47 and remainder ten gives 7.

quiz.prompt: Which encoded key corresponds to original -99?
quiz.explanation: The smallest allowed original key maps to zero.

quiz.prompt: How many fixed decimal passes run for places 1, 10 and 100?
quiz.explanation: The loop executes three places before place becomes 1000.

keyPoints.en: LSD processes digits from low to high.
keyPoints.bn: LSD-তে ছোট place-এর digit আগে আসে।

keyPoints.en: Each digit pass must preserve ties.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি digit pass-এ সমান digit-এর ক্রম থাকতে হবে।

keyPoints.en: Define signed-key encoding before extracting digits.
keyPoints.bn: Digit নেওয়ার আগে signed key-এর encoding ঠিক করো।

keyPoints.en: General cost includes digit count and base.
keyPoints.bn: সাধারণ খরচে digit-এর সংখ্যা আর base ধরো।

keyPoints.en: Reuse the output buffer between passes.
keyPoints.bn: একই output buffer পরের pass-এ আবার ব্যবহার করো।
